title: Analytic proof search for propositional sequents

based_on.title: Proof Theory: Foundations and Applications (June 2013 lecture notes)
based_on.pages: Section 1.2 pp. 7–8 (invertible rules, completeness by connective count); section 1.3 pp. 9–12 (subformula consequences).

summary: A deterministic decomposition of a presented finite sequent returns a primitive proof or a concrete countervaluation, and decides numbered-atom classical consequence.
abstract: A finite propositional problem can be settled by exposing one connective at a time. We give a procedure that either builds a proof in the one-sided sequent calculus or returns an assignment making every proposed alternative false. It keeps already processed literals beside an ordered list of formulas, splits conjunctions into two proof obligations, and closes a branch when opposite literals meet. A decreasing formula weight proves that every run ends, while explicit reconstruction turns successful branches into finite proofs. The same procedure decides ordinary classical consequences after the specified translation of hypotheses and conclusion, including empty inputs, constants, and repeated formulas.
